```cobol
           05 IN-CUST-DATE        PIC 9(8).

       FD  OUTFILE

           RECORD CONTAINS 100 CHARACTERS.
       01  OUT-RECORD             PIC X(100).
       
       FD  ERRFILE
           RECORDING MODE IS F
           RECORD CONTAINS 150 CHARACTERS.
       01  ERR-RECORD.
           05 ERR-ORIGINAL        PIC X(100).
           05 ERR-CODE            PIC X(4).
           05 ERR-MESSAGE         PIC X(46).
       
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01  WS-FILE-STATUS.
           05 WS-INFILE-STATUS    PIC XX.
           05 WS-OUTFILE-STATUS   PIC XX.
           05 WS-ERRFILE-STATUS   PIC XX.
       
       01  WS-FLAGS.
           05 WS-EOF-FLAG         PIC X(1) VALUE 'N'.
              88 END-OF-FILE      VALUE 'Y'.
              88 NOT-END-OF-FILE  VALUE 'N'.
           05 WS-VALID-FLAG       PIC X(1).
              88 RECORD-VALID     VALUE 'Y'.
              88 RECORD-INVALID   VALUE 'N'.
       
       01  WS-COUNTERS.
           05 WS-READ-COUNT       PIC 9(9) VALUE 0.
           05 WS-VALID-COUNT      PIC 9(9) VALUE 0.
           05 WS-ERROR-COUNT      PIC 9(9) VALUE 0.
       
       01  WS-WORK-AREAS.
           05 WS-CURRENT-DATE     PIC 9(8).
           05 WS-ERROR-CODE       PIC X(4).
           05 WS-ERROR-MSG        PIC X(46).
       
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       0000-MAIN.
           PERFORM 1000-INITIALIZE
           PERFORM 2000-PROCESS UNTIL END-OF-FILE
           PERFORM 9000-TERMINATE
           STOP RUN.
       
       1000-INITIALIZE.
           OPEN INPUT  INFILE
           OPEN OUTPUT OUTFILE
           OPEN OUTPUT ERRFILE
           
           IF WS-INFILE-STATUS NOT = '00'
               DISPLAY 'ERROR OPENING INPUT FILE: ' WS-INFILE-STATUS
               MOVE 8 TO RETURN-CODE
               STOP RUN
           END-IF
           
           ACCEPT WS-CURRENT-DATE FROM DATE YYYYMMDD
           
           PERFORM 1100-READ-INPUT.
       
       1100-READ-INPUT.
           READ INFILE
               AT END SET END-OF-FILE TO TRUE
               NOT AT END ADD 1 TO WS-READ-COUNT
           END-READ.
       
       2000-PROCESS.
           PERFORM 2100-VALIDATE-RECORD
           
           IF RECORD-VALID
               PERFORM 2200-WRITE-VALID
           ELSE
               PERFORM 2300-WRITE-ERROR
           END-IF
           
           PERFORM 1100-READ-INPUT.
       
       2100-VALIDATE-RECORD.
           SET RECORD-VALID TO TRUE
           INITIALIZE WS-ERROR-CODE WS-ERROR-MSG
           
           IF IN-CUST-ID = SPACES OR IN-CUST-ID = LOW-VALUES
               SET RECORD-INVALID TO TRUE
               MOVE 'E001' TO WS-ERROR-CODE
               MOVE 'CUSTOMER ID IS BLANK' TO WS-ERROR-MSG
           END-IF
           
           IF RECORD-VALID AND IN-CUST-BALANCE NOT NUMERIC
               SET RECORD-INVALID TO TRUE
               MOVE 'E002' TO WS-ERROR-CODE
               MOVE 'BALANCE IS NOT NUMERIC' TO WS-ERROR-MSG
           END-IF
           
           IF RECORD-VALID AND IN-CUST-STATUS NOT = 'A' AND 'I' AND 'C'
               SET RECORD-INVALID TO TRUE
               MOVE 'E003' TO WS-ERROR-CODE
               MOVE 'INVALID STATUS CODE' TO WS-ERROR-MSG
           END-IF
           
           IF RECORD-VALID AND IN-CUST-DATE > WS-CURRENT-DATE
               SET RECORD-INVALID TO TRUE
               MOVE 'E004' TO WS-ERROR-CODE
               MOVE 'DATE IS IN THE FUTURE' TO WS-ERROR-MSG
           END-IF.
       
       2200-WRITE-VALID.
           MOVE IN-RECORD TO OUT-RECORD
           WRITE OUT-RECORD
           ADD 1 TO WS-VALID-COUNT.
       
       2300-WRITE-ERROR.
           MOVE IN-RECORD TO ERR-ORIGINAL
           MOVE WS-ERROR-CODE TO ERR-CODE
           MOVE WS-ERROR-MSG TO ERR-MESSAGE
           WRITE ERR-RECORD
           ADD 1 TO WS-ERROR-COUNT.
       
       9000-TERMINATE.
           CLOSE INFILE OUTFILE ERRFILE
           
           DISPLAY '=================================='
           DISPLAY 'PROCESSING COMPLETE'
           DISPLAY '=================================='
           DISPLAY 'RECORDS READ:    ' WS-READ-COUNT
           DISPLAY 'RECORDS VALID:   ' WS-VALID-COUNT
           DISPLAY 'RECORDS IN ERROR:' WS-ERROR-COUNT
           DISPLAY '=================================='.
```

```cobol
           05 CUST-NAME-KEY       PIC X(30).

           05 CUST-STATUS         PIC X(1).
           05 FILLER              PIC X(50).
       
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01  WS-VSAM-STATUS         PIC XX.
           88 VSAM-OK             VALUE '00'.
           88 VSAM-EOF            VALUE '10'.
           88 VSAM-DUPKEY         VALUE '22'.
           88 VSAM-NOTFND         VALUE '23'.
           88 VSAM-NOSPACE        VALUE '24'.
       
       01  WS-VSAM-FEEDBACK       PIC 9(3).
       
       01  WS-FUNCTION            PIC X(6).
           88 FUNC-READ           VALUE 'READ'.
           88 FUNC-WRITE          VALUE 'WRITE'.
           88 FUNC-REWRITE        VALUE 'REWRIT'.
           88 FUNC-DELETE         VALUE 'DELETE'.
           88 FUNC-START          VALUE 'START'.
       
       01  WS-SEARCH-KEY          PIC X(10).
       01  WS-RECORDS-PROCESSED   PIC 9(7) VALUE 0.
       
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       0000-MAIN.
           PERFORM 1000-OPEN-FILE
           PERFORM 2000-PROCESS-REQUESTS
           PERFORM 9000-CLOSE-FILE
           STOP RUN.
       
       1000-OPEN-FILE.
           OPEN I-O CUSTOMER-FILE
           IF NOT VSAM-OK
               PERFORM 8000-VSAM-ERROR
               MOVE 12 TO RETURN-CODE
               STOP RUN
           END-IF.
       
       2000-PROCESS-REQUESTS.
      *    Example: Read by key
           MOVE 'CUST000001' TO CUST-KEY
           MOVE 'READ' TO WS-FUNCTION
           PERFORM 3000-READ-RANDOM
           
      *    Example: Browse all records
           PERFORM 4000-BROWSE-FILE
           
      *    Example: Update a record
           MOVE 'REWRIT' TO WS-FUNCTION
           ADD 100.00 TO CUST-BALANCE
           PERFORM 5000-UPDATE-RECORD.
       
       3000-READ-RANDOM.
           READ CUSTOMER-FILE
               INVALID KEY
                   PERFORM 8100-HANDLE-READ-ERROR
               NOT INVALID KEY
                   ADD 1 TO WS-RECORDS-PROCESSED
                   DISPLAY 'FOUND: ' CUST-KEY ' ' CUST-NAME-KEY
           END-READ.
       
       4000-BROWSE-FILE.
           MOVE LOW-VALUES TO CUST-KEY
           MOVE 'START' TO WS-FUNCTION
           START CUSTOMER-FILE KEY >= CUST-KEY
               INVALID KEY
                   DISPLAY 'FILE IS EMPTY'
                   GO TO 4000-EXIT
           END-START
           
           PERFORM UNTIL VSAM-EOF
               READ CUSTOMER-FILE NEXT
                   AT END
                       CONTINUE
                   NOT AT END
                       DISPLAY CUST-KEY ' ' CUST-NAME-KEY 
                               ' BAL=' CUST-BALANCE
               END-READ
           END-PERFORM.
       4000-EXIT.
           EXIT.
       
       5000-UPDATE-RECORD.
           REWRITE CUSTOMER-RECORD
               INVALID KEY
                   PERFORM 8200-HANDLE-WRITE-ERROR
               NOT INVALID KEY
                   DISPLAY 'RECORD UPDATED: ' CUST-KEY
           END-REWRITE.
       
       6000-ADD-RECORD.
           WRITE CUSTOMER-RECORD
               INVALID KEY
                   IF VSAM-DUPKEY
                       DISPLAY 'DUPLICATE KEY: ' CUST-KEY
                   ELSE IF VSAM-NOSPACE
                       DISPLAY 'FILE IS FULL'
                   ELSE
                       PERFORM 8200-HANDLE-WRITE-ERROR
                   END-IF
               NOT INVALID KEY
                   DISPLAY 'RECORD ADDED: ' CUST-KEY
           END-WRITE.
       
       7000-DELETE-RECORD.
           DELETE CUSTOMER-FILE
               INVALID KEY
                   PERFORM 8100-HANDLE-READ-ERROR
               NOT INVALID KEY
                   DISPLAY 'RECORD DELETED: ' CUST-KEY
           END-DELETE.
       
       8000-VSAM-ERROR.
           DISPLAY '*** VSAM ERROR ***'
           DISPLAY 'FUNCTION: ' WS-FUNCTION
           DISPLAY 'STATUS:   ' WS-VSAM-STATUS
           DISPLAY 'FEEDBACK: ' WS-VSAM-FEEDBACK
           EVALUATE WS-VSAM-STATUS
               WHEN '00' DISPLAY 'SUCCESSFUL'
               WHEN '10' DISPLAY 'END OF FILE'
               WHEN '22' DISPLAY 'DUPLICATE KEY'
               WHEN '23' DISPLAY 'RECORD NOT FOUND'
               WHEN '24' DISPLAY 'NO SPACE ON VOLUME'
               WHEN '35' DISPLAY 'FILE NOT FOUND'
               WHEN '39' DISPLAY 'FILE MISMATCH'
               WHEN '41' DISPLAY 'FILE ALREADY OPEN'
               WHEN '42' DISPLAY 'FILE NOT OPEN'
               WHEN '46' DISPLAY 'NO VALID NEXT RECORD'
               WHEN '47' DISPLAY 'READ NOT ALLOWED'
               WHEN '48' DISPLAY 'WRITE NOT ALLOWED'
               WHEN '49' DISPLAY 'REWRITE/DELETE NOT ALLOWED'
               WHEN OTHER DISPLAY 'UNKNOWN ERROR'
           END-EVALUATE.
       
       8100-HANDLE-READ-ERROR.
           IF VSAM-NOTFND
               DISPLAY 'RECORD NOT FOUND: ' CUST-KEY
           ELSE
               PERFORM 8000-VSAM-ERROR
           END-IF.
       
       8200-HANDLE-WRITE-ERROR.
           PERFORM 8000-VSAM-ERROR.
       
       9000-CLOSE-FILE.
           CLOSE CUSTOMER-FILE.
```

```cobol
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. DB2BATCH.
      *================================================================*
      * DB2 Batch Processing with Cursor and Commit Point Logic        *
      *================================================================*
       
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       
           EXEC SQL INCLUDE SQLCA END-EXEC.
           EXEC SQL INCLUDE CUSTOMER END-EXEC.
       
       01  WS-SQLCODE             PIC S9(9) COMP VALUE 0.
       01  WS-COMMIT-COUNT        PIC 9(5) VALUE 0.
       01  WS-COMMIT-FREQUENCY    PIC 9(5) VALUE 1000.
       01  WS-TOTAL-PROCESSED     PIC 9(9) VALUE 0.
       01  WS-TOTAL-UPDATED       PIC 9(9) VALUE 0.
       01  WS-TOTAL-ERRORS        PIC 9(9) VALUE 0.
       
       01  WS-CURRENT-TIMESTAMP.
           05 WS-CURR-DATE        PIC X(10).
           05 FILLER              PIC X(1) VALUE '-'.
           05 WS-CURR-TIME        PIC X(8).
       
       01  WS-HOST-VARIABLES.
           05 HV-CUST-ID          PIC X(10).
           05 HV-CUST-NAME        PIC X(50).
           05 HV-BALANCE          PIC S9(9)V99 COMP-3.
           05 HV-STATUS           PIC X(1).
           05 HV-LAST-UPDATE      PIC X(26).
       
       01  WS-NULL-INDICATORS.
           05 NI-CUST-NAME        PIC S9(4) COMP.
           05 NI-BALANCE          PIC S9(4) COMP.
       
           EXEC SQL DECLARE CUST_CURSOR CURSOR WITH HOLD FOR
               SELECT CUST_ID,
                      CUST_NAME,
                      BALANCE,
                      STATUS,
                      LAST_UPDATE
               FROM CUSTOMER_TABLE
               WHERE STATUS = 'A'
                 AND BALANCE > 0
               FOR UPDATE OF BALANCE, LAST_UPDATE
           END-EXEC.
       
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       0000-MAIN.
           PERFORM 1000-INITIALIZE
           PERFORM 2000-PROCESS-CUSTOMERS
           PERFORM 9000-TERMINATE
           GOBACK.
       
       1000-INITIALIZE.
           DISPLAY 'DB2BATCH STARTED'
           EXEC SQL
               SELECT CURRENT TIMESTAMP
               INTO :WS-CURRENT-TIMESTAMP
               FROM SYSIBM.SYSDUMMY1
           END-EXEC
           
           DISPLAY 'PROCESSING TIME: ' WS-CURRENT-TIMESTAMP
           
           EXEC SQL OPEN CUST_CURSOR END-EXEC
           IF SQLCODE NOT = 0
               DISPLAY 'ERROR OPENING CURSOR: ' SQLCODE
               PERFORM 8000-DB2-ERROR
               MOVE 12 TO RETURN-CODE
               GOBACK
           END-IF.
       
       2000-PROCESS-CUSTOMERS.
           PERFORM 2100-FETCH-CUSTOMER
           PERFORM UNTIL SQLCODE = 100
               PERFORM 2200-UPDATE-CUSTOMER
               PERFORM 2300-CHECK-COMMIT
               PERFORM 2100-FETCH-CUSTOMER
           END-PERFORM.
       
       2100-FETCH-CUSTOMER.
           EXEC SQL
               FETCH CUST_CURSOR
               INTO :HV-CUST-ID,
                    :HV-CUST-NAME :NI-CUST-NAME,
                    :HV-BALANCE   :NI-BALANCE,
                    :HV-STATUS,
                    :HV-LAST-UPDATE
           END-EXEC
           
           MOVE SQLCODE TO WS-SQLCODE
           
           IF SQLCODE = 0
               ADD 1 TO WS-TOTAL-PROCESSED
           ELSE IF SQLCODE NOT = 100
               PERFORM 8000-DB2-ERROR
           END-IF.
       
       2200-UPDATE-CUSTOMER.
      *    Apply 2% interest to positive balances
           IF HV-BALANCE > 0
               COMPUTE HV-BALANCE = HV-BALANCE * 1.02
               
               EXEC SQL
                   UPDATE CUSTOMER_TABLE
                   SET BALANCE = :HV-BALANCE,
                       LAST_UPDATE = CURRENT TIMESTAMP
                   WHERE CURRENT OF CUST_CURSOR
               END-EXEC
               
               IF SQLCODE = 0
                   ADD 1 TO WS-TOTAL-UPDATED
                   ADD 1 TO WS-COMMIT-COUNT
               ELSE
                   ADD 1 TO WS-TOTAL-ERRORS
                   DISPLAY 'UPDATE ERROR FOR: ' HV-CUST-ID
                   PERFORM 8000-DB2-ERROR
               END-IF
           END-IF.
       
       2300-CHECK-COMMIT.
           IF WS-COMMIT-COUNT >= WS-COMMIT-FREQUENCY
               EXEC SQL COMMIT END-EXEC
               IF SQLCODE = 0
                   DISPLAY 'COMMIT AT: ' WS-TOTAL-PROCESSED ' RECORDS'
                   MOVE 0 TO WS-COMMIT-COUNT
               ELSE
                   DISPLAY 'COMMIT FAILED'
                   PERFORM 8000-DB2-ERROR
                   EXEC SQL ROLLBACK END-EXEC
                   MOVE 16 TO RETURN-CODE
                   GOBACK
               END-IF
           END-IF.
       
       8000-DB2-ERROR.
           DISPLAY '*** DB2 ERROR ***'
           DISPLAY 'SQLCODE:  ' SQLCODE
           DISPLAY 'SQLERRMC: ' SQLERRMC
           DISPLAY 'SQLERRD:  ' SQLERRD(3)
           
           EVALUATE SQLCODE
               WHEN 0     DISPLAY 'SUCCESSFUL'
               WHEN 100   DISPLAY 'NOT FOUND / END OF DATA'
               WHEN -803  DISPLAY 'DUPLICATE KEY'
               WHEN -811  DISPLAY 'MORE THAN ONE ROW'
               WHEN -818  DISPLAY 'TIMESTAMP MISMATCH'
               WHEN -904  DISPLAY 'RESOURCE UNAVAILABLE'
               WHEN -911  DISPLAY 'DEADLOCK OR TIMEOUT'
               WHEN -913  DISPLAY 'DEADLOCK VICTIM'
               WHEN OTHER DISPLAY 'CHECK DB2 CODES MANUAL'
           END-EVALUATE.
       
       9000-TERMINATE.
           EXEC SQL CLOSE CUST_CURSOR END-EXEC
           EXEC SQL COMMIT END-EXEC
           
           DISPLAY '=================================='
           DISPLAY 'DB2BATCH COMPLETE'
           DISPLAY '=================================='
           DISPLAY 'RECORDS PROCESSED: ' WS-TOTAL-PROCESSED
           DISPLAY 'RECORDS UPDATED:   ' WS-TOTAL-UPDATED
           DISPLAY 'ERRORS:            ' WS-TOTAL-ERRORS
           DISPLAY '=================================='.
```

```cobol
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. CUSTINQ.
      *================================================================*
      * CICS Customer Inquiry Program with BMS Map                     *
      *================================================================*
       
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       
       01  WS-COMMAREA.
           05 WS-COMM-STATE       PIC X(2).
              88 STATE-INITIAL    VALUE 'IN'.
              88 STATE-DISPLAY    VALUE 'DS'.
              88 STATE-UPDATE     VALUE 'UP'.
           05 WS-COMM-CUST-ID     PIC X(10).
           05 WS-COMM-MSG         PIC X(50).
       
       01  WS-RESPONSE            PIC S9(8) COMP.
       01  WS-RESPONSE2           PIC S9(8) COMP.
       
       01  WS-CUSTOMER-RECORD.
           05 WS-CUST-ID          PIC X(10).
           05 WS-CUST-NAME        PIC X(30).
           05 WS-CUST-ADDR        PIC X(50).
           05 WS-CUST-PHONE       PIC X(15).
           05 WS-CUST-BALANCE     PIC S9(9)V99 COMP-3.
           05 WS-CUST-STATUS      PIC X(1).
       
       COPY CUSTMAP.
       
       LINKAGE SECTION.
       01  DFHCOMMAREA            PIC X(62).
       
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       0000-MAIN.
           EVALUATE TRUE
               WHEN EIBCALEN = 0
                   PERFORM 1000-FIRST-TIME
               WHEN EIBAID = DFHCLEAR
                   PERFORM 9000-RETURN-TRANS
               WHEN EIBAID = DFHPF3
                   PERFORM 9100-END-SESSION
               WHEN EIBAID = DFHENTER
                   PERFORM 2000-PROCESS-INPUT
               WHEN EIBAID = DFHPF5
                   PERFORM 3000-UPDATE-RECORD
               WHEN OTHER
                   MOVE 'INVALID KEY PRESSED' TO WS-COMM-MSG
                   PERFORM 4000-SEND-MAP
           END-EVALUATE
           
           PERFORM 9000-RETURN-TRANS.
       
       1000-FIRST-TIME.
           INITIALIZE CUSTMAPO
           MOVE 'ENTER CUSTOMER ID AND PRESS ENTER' TO MSGO
           SET STATE-INITIAL TO TRUE
           PERFORM 4100-SEND-MAP-ERASE.
       
       2000-PROCESS-INPUT.
           PERFORM 2100-RECEIVE-MAP
           
           IF CUSTIDI = SPACES OR CUSTIDI = LOW-VALUES
               MOVE 'CUSTOMER ID IS REQUIRED' TO MSGO
               MOVE -1 TO CUSTIDL
               PERFORM 4200-SEND-MAP-DATAONLY
               GO TO 2000-EXIT
           END-IF
           
           MOVE CUSTIDI TO WS-CUST-ID
           PERFORM 2200-READ-CUSTOMER
           
           IF WS-RESPONSE = DFHRESP(NORMAL)
               PERFORM 2300-DISPLAY-CUSTOMER
               SET STATE-DISPLAY TO TRUE
           ELSE
               MOVE 'CUSTOMER NOT FOUND' TO MSGO
               MOVE -1 TO CUSTIDL
               PERFORM 4200-SEND-MAP-DATAONLY
           END-IF.
       2000-EXIT.
           EXIT.
       
       2100-RECEIVE-MAP.
           EXEC CICS RECEIVE MAP('CUSTMAP')
               MAPSET('CUSTSET')
               INTO(CUSTMAPI)
               RESP(WS-RESPONSE)
               RESP2(WS-RESPONSE2)
           END-EXEC
           
           IF WS-RESPONSE NOT = DFHRESP(NORMAL)
               IF WS-RESPONSE = DFHRESP(MAPFAIL)
                   MOVE 'NO DATA ENTERED' TO MSGO
               ELSE
                   PERFORM 8000-CICS-ERROR
               END-IF
           END-IF.
       
       2200-READ-CUSTOMER.
           EXEC CICS READ FILE('CUSTFILE')
               INTO(WS-CUSTOMER-RECORD)
               RIDFLD(WS-CUST-ID)
               RESP(WS-RESPONSE)
               RESP2(WS-RESPONSE2)
           END-EXEC.
       
       2300-DISPLAY-CUSTOMER.
           MOVE WS-CUST-ID      TO CUSTIDO
           MOVE WS-CUST-NAME    TO NAMEO
           MOVE WS-CUST-ADDR    TO ADDRO
           MOVE WS-CUST-PHONE   TO PHONEO
           MOVE WS-CUST-BALANCE TO BALANCEO
           MOVE WS-CUST-STATUS  TO STATUSO
           MOVE 'RECORD FOUND - PF5 TO UPDATE, PF3 TO EXIT' TO MSGO
           PERFORM 4200-SEND-MAP-DATAONLY.
       
       3000-UPDATE-RECORD.
           IF NOT STATE-DISPLAY
               MOVE 'DISPLAY RECORD FIRST' TO MSGO
               PERFORM 4200-SEND-MAP-DATAONLY
               GO TO 3000-EXIT
           END-IF
           
           PERFORM 2100-RECEIVE-MAP
           PERFORM 3100-VALIDATE-INPUT
           
           IF WS-RESPONSE = DFHRESP(NORMAL)
               PERFORM 3200-REWRITE-RECORD
           END-IF.
       3000-EXIT.
           EXIT.
       
       3100-VALIDATE-INPUT.
           MOVE DFHRESP(NORMAL) TO WS-RESPONSE
           
           IF NAMEI = SPACES
               MOVE 'NAME IS REQUIRED' TO MSGO
               MOVE -1 TO NAMEL
               MOVE DFHRESP(ERROR) TO WS-RESPONSE
           END-IF.
       
       3200-REWRITE-RECORD.
           MOVE NAMEI    TO WS-CUST-NAME
           MOVE ADDRI    TO WS-CUST-ADDR
           MOVE PHONEI   TO WS-CUST-PHONE
           MOVE STATUSI  TO WS-CUST-STATUS
           
           EXEC CICS READ FILE('CUSTFILE')
               INTO(WS-CUSTOMER-RECORD)
               RIDFLD(WS-CUST-ID)
               UPDATE
               RESP(WS-RESPONSE)
           END-EXEC
           
           IF WS-RESPONSE = DFHRESP(NORMAL)
               EXEC CICS REWRITE FILE('CUSTFILE')
                   FROM(WS-CUSTOMER-RECORD)
                   RESP(WS-RESPONSE)
               END-EXEC
               
               IF WS-RESPONSE = DFHRESP(NORMAL)
                   MOVE 'RECORD UPDATED SUCCESSFULLY' TO MSGO
               ELSE
                   PERFORM 8000-CICS-ERROR
               END-IF
           ELSE
               PERFORM 8000-CICS-ERROR
           END-IF
           
           PERFORM 4200-SEND-MAP-DATAONLY.
       
       4000-SEND-MAP.
           EXEC CICS SEND MAP('CUSTMAP')
               MAPSET('CUSTSET')
               FROM(CUSTMAPO)
               RESP(WS-RESPONSE)
           END-EXEC.
       
       4100-SEND-MAP-ERASE.
           EXEC CICS SEND MAP('CUSTMAP')
               MAPSET('CUSTSET')
               FROM(CUSTMAPO)
               ERASE
               RESP(WS-RESPONSE)
           END-EXEC.
       
       4200-SEND-MAP-DATAONLY.
           EXEC CICS SEND MAP('CUSTMAP')
               MAPSET('CUSTSET')
               FROM(CUSTMAPO)
               DATAONLY
               CURSOR
               RESP(WS-RESPONSE)
           END-EXEC.
       
       8000-CICS-ERROR.
           MOVE 'CICS ERROR OCCURRED' TO MSGO
           STRING 'RESP=' DELIMITED SIZE
                  WS-RESPONSE DELIMITED SIZE
                  ' RESP2=' DELIMITED SIZE
                  WS-RESPONSE2 DELIMITED SIZE
               INTO MSGO
           END-STRING.
       
       9000-RETURN-TRANS.
           EXEC CICS RETURN
               TRANSID('CINQ')
               COMMAREA(WS-COMMAREA)
               LENGTH(LENGTH OF WS-COMMAREA)
           END-EXEC.
       
       9100-END-SESSION.
           EXEC CICS SEND TEXT
               FROM('SESSION ENDED - GOODBYE')
               ERASE
           END-EXEC
           EXEC CICS RETURN END-EXEC.
```

Explain COBOL COMP, COMP-3, COMP-5 data types with examples

In COBOL, computational data types control how numbers are stored in memory:

**COMP (COMP-4) - Binary**
```cobol
01  WS-BINARY-2         PIC S9(4)  COMP.   * 2 bytes (halfword)
01  WS-BINARY-4         PIC S9(9)  COMP.   * 4 bytes (fullword)
01  WS-BINARY-8         PIC S9(18) COMP.   * 8 bytes (doubleword)
```
- Stored as pure binary (twos complement for signed)
- S9(4) = -32768 to +32767
- Fast arithmetic, used for subscripts and counters

**COMP-3 - Packed Decimal**
```cobol
01  WS-PACKED-AMOUNT    PIC S9(7)V99 COMP-3.  * 5 bytes
01  WS-PACKED-RATE      PIC S9(3)V9(4) COMP-3. * 4 bytes
```
- Each byte holds 2 digits, last nibble is sign (C=+, D=-)
- Formula: (digits + 1) / 2 rounded up
- S9(7)V99 = 9 digits = 5 bytes
- Best for dollar amounts and calculations

**COMP-5 - Native Binary**
```cobol
01  WS-NATIVE           PIC S9(9) COMP-5.
```
- Like COMP but uses full binary range
- PIC S9(4) can exceed 9999 (up to 32767)
- Faster on some platforms

**DISPLAY (default)**
```cobol
01  WS-DISPLAY          PIC 9(5)V99.  * 7 bytes (zoned decimal)
```
- One byte per digit
- Human readable in dumps
- Slower arithmetic

**Best Practices:**
```cobol
* Use COMP for subscripts and counters
01  WS-INDEX            PIC S9(4) COMP VALUE 0.

* Use COMP-3 for money and calculations  
01  WS-AMOUNT           PIC S9(9)V99 COMP-3 VALUE 0.

* Use DISPLAY for fields written to files/reports
01  WS-REPORT-AMT       PIC Z,ZZZ,ZZ9.99-.
```

```cobol
           05 WS-MONTHLY-RATE     PIC S9V9(8) COMP-3.
           05 WS-POWER            PIC S9(5)V9(8) COMP-3.
           05 WS-NUMERATOR        PIC S9(15)V99 COMP-3.
           05 WS-DENOMINATOR      PIC S9(15)V99 COMP-3.
           05 WS-TEMP-RESULT      PIC S9(15)V99 COMP-3.
       
       01  WS-ERROR-FLAGS.
           05 WS-OVERFLOW-FLAG    PIC X VALUE 'N'.
              88 OVERFLOW-OCCURRED VALUE 'Y'.
           05 WS-DIVIDE-FLAG      PIC X VALUE 'N'.
              88 DIVIDE-BY-ZERO   VALUE 'Y'.
       
       01  WS-DISPLAY-FIELDS.
           05 WS-DISP-PRINCIPAL   PIC $$$,$$$,$$9.99.
           05 WS-DISP-PAYMENT     PIC $$$,$$9.99.
           05 WS-DISP-INTEREST    PIC $$$,$$$,$$9.99.
       
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       0000-MAIN.
           MOVE 250000.00 TO WS-PRINCIPAL
           MOVE .065 TO WS-INTEREST-RATE
           MOVE 360 TO WS-TERM-MONTHS
           
           PERFORM 1000-CALCULATE-PAYMENT
           PERFORM 2000-DISPLAY-RESULTS
           STOP RUN.
       
       1000-CALCULATE-PAYMENT.
      *    Monthly payment = P * [r(1+r)^n] / [(1+r)^n - 1]
      *    Where: P=principal, r=monthly rate, n=months
           
           INITIALIZE WS-ERROR-FLAGS
           
      *    Calculate monthly rate
           IF WS-INTEREST-RATE = 0
               COMPUTE WS-MONTHLY-PAYMENT ROUNDED =
                   WS-PRINCIPAL / WS-TERM-MONTHS
               GO TO 1000-EXIT
           END-IF
           
           COMPUTE WS-MONTHLY-RATE = WS-INTEREST-RATE / 12
           
      *    Calculate (1 + r)^n with overflow check
           COMPUTE WS-POWER = (1 + WS-MONTHLY-RATE) 
                              ** WS-TERM-MONTHS
               ON SIZE ERROR
                   SET OVERFLOW-OCCURRED TO TRUE
                   DISPLAY 'OVERFLOW IN POWER CALCULATION'
                   GO TO 1000-EXIT
           END-COMPUTE
           
      *    Calculate numerator: r * (1+r)^n
           COMPUTE WS-NUMERATOR = 
               WS-MONTHLY-RATE * WS-POWER
               ON SIZE ERROR
                   SET OVERFLOW-OCCURRED TO TRUE
           END-COMPUTE
           
      *    Calculate denominator: (1+r)^n - 1
           COMPUTE WS-DENOMINATOR = WS-POWER - 1
           
           IF WS-DENOMINATOR = 0
               SET DIVIDE-BY-ZERO TO TRUE
               DISPLAY 'DIVIDE BY ZERO ERROR'
               GO TO 1000-EXIT
           END-IF
           
      *    Final calculation
           COMPUTE WS-MONTHLY-PAYMENT ROUNDED =
               WS-PRINCIPAL * (WS-NUMERATOR / WS-DENOMINATOR)
               ON SIZE ERROR
                   SET OVERFLOW-OCCURRED TO TRUE
           END-COMPUTE
           
      *    Calculate total interest
           COMPUTE WS-TOTAL-INTEREST =
               (WS-MONTHLY-PAYMENT * WS-TERM-MONTHS) - WS-PRINCIPAL.
       
       1000-EXIT.
           EXIT.
       
       2000-DISPLAY-RESULTS.
           IF OVERFLOW-OCCURRED OR DIVIDE-BY-ZERO
               DISPLAY 'CALCULATION ERROR OCCURRED'
           ELSE
               MOVE WS-PRINCIPAL TO WS-DISP-PRINCIPAL
               MOVE WS-MONTHLY-PAYMENT TO WS-DISP-PAYMENT
               MOVE WS-TOTAL-INTEREST TO WS-DISP-INTEREST
               
               DISPLAY 'LOAN AMORTIZATION'
               DISPLAY '================='
               DISPLAY 'PRINCIPAL:       ' WS-DISP-PRINCIPAL
               DISPLAY 'MONTHLY PAYMENT: ' WS-DISP-PAYMENT
               DISPLAY 'TOTAL INTEREST:  ' WS-DISP-INTEREST
           END-IF.
```

```cobol
           MOVE '***-**-' TO WS-EXTRACT
           STRING WS-EXTRACT DELIMITED SIZE
                  WS-SSN(8:4) DELIMITED SIZE
               INTO WS-EXTRACT
      *    Result: "***-**-6789"
           
      *    Extract area code from phone
           MOVE WS-PHONE(2:3) TO WS-EXTRACT
      *    Result: "555"
           
      *    Variable positions
           MOVE 6 TO WS-START
           MOVE 6 TO WS-LENGTH
           MOVE WS-FULL-NAME(WS-START:WS-LENGTH) TO WS-EXTRACT
      *    Result: "QUINCY"
           
      *    Parse delimited string
           INSPECT WS-FULL-NAME TALLYING WS-START
               FOR CHARACTERS BEFORE INITIAL SPACE
           ADD 1 TO WS-START
           MOVE WS-FULL-NAME(WS-START:) TO WS-EXTRACT
      *    Result: " QUINCY ADAMS" (from first space to end)
           
      *    Right-justify using reference modification
           MOVE FUNCTION LENGTH(FUNCTION TRIM(WS-EXTRACT))
               TO WS-LENGTH
           COMPUTE WS-START = 20 - WS-LENGTH + 1
           MOVE SPACES TO WS-EXTRACT
           MOVE FUNCTION TRIM(WS-FULL-NAME) 
               TO WS-EXTRACT(WS-START:WS-LENGTH)
```

**Key Points:**
- Start position is 1-based
- Length is optional (defaults to remaining length)
- Both can be literals or variables
- Can be used on either side of MOVE
- Works with group and elementary items

```cobol
      * LINK: Returns to caller (like CALL)                            *

      *================================================================*
       
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.

           EVALUATE TRUE
               WHEN EIBCALEN = 0
                   PERFORM 1000-MAIN-MENU
               WHEN OTHER
                   PERFORM 2000-PROCESS-REQUEST
           END-EVALUATE
           
           EXEC CICS RETURN END-EXEC.

      *    Using LINK - control returns here after subprogram

           MOVE 'INIT' TO WS-FUNCTION
           MOVE 'CUST001' TO WS-CUSTOMER-ID
           MOVE LENGTH OF WS-COMMAREA TO WS-COMMAREA-LEN

               PROGRAM('CUSTINQ')
               COMMAREA(WS-COMMAREA)
               LENGTH(WS-COMMAREA-LEN)

      *        Control returns here after CUSTINQ completes
               IF WS-RETURN-CODE = 0

                   PERFORM 1100-SHOW-DETAILS
               ELSE

               END-IF
           ELSE IF WS-RESPONSE = DFHRESP(PGMIDERR)
               DISPLAY 'PROGRAM NOT FOUND: CUSTINQ'
           ELSE
               DISPLAY 'LINK ERROR: ' WS-RESPONSE
           END-IF.

      *    Using XCTL - control does NOT return here
      *    XCTL is used when this program's work is done
           MOVE 'DETAIL' TO WS-FUNCTION
           MOVE LENGTH OF WS-COMMAREA TO WS-COMMAREA-LEN
           
           EXEC CICS XCTL
               PROGRAM('CUSTDET')
               COMMAREA(WS-COMMAREA)
               LENGTH(WS-COMMAREA-LEN)
               RESP(WS-RESPONSE)
           END-EXEC
           
      *    If we get here, XCTL failed
           DISPLAY 'XCTL FAILED: ' WS-RESPONSE.
       
       2000-PROCESS-REQUEST.
      *    Handle dynamic program selection
           EVALUATE WS-FUNCTION OF DFHCOMMAREA
               WHEN 'INQR'
                   MOVE 'CUSTINQ' TO WS-PROGRAM-NAME
               WHEN 'UPDT'
                   MOVE 'CUSTUPD' TO WS-PROGRAM-NAME
               WHEN 'DELT'
                   MOVE 'CUSTDEL' TO WS-PROGRAM-NAME
               WHEN OTHER

           END-EVALUATE
           
      *    Dynamic LINK with variable program name

               PROGRAM(WS-PROGRAM-NAME)

           END-EXEC.
```

**Key Differences:**

| Aspect | LINK | XCTL |
|--------|------|------|
| Returns to caller | Yes | No |
| Storage preserved | Yes | Released |
| Use case | Subroutine call | Menu navigation |
| Stack usage | Adds to stack | Replaces current |
| Performance | Slightly slower | Faster |

**Best Practices:**
- Use LINK for reusable modules (validation, formatting)
- Use XCTL for screen navigation (menu to detail)
- Avoid deep LINK nesting (max 8-10 levels)
- Use COMMAREA to pass data between programs

```cobol
       01  WS-OUTPUT-STR         PIC X(100).
       
      *    USE INDEXED TABLES FOR LOOKUPS
       01  WS-LOOKUP-TABLE.
           05 WS-ENTRY OCCURS 1000 TIMES
              ASCENDING KEY IS WS-LOOKUP-KEY
              INDEXED BY WS-TBL-IDX.
               10 WS-LOOKUP-KEY   PIC X(10).
               10 WS-LOOKUP-VALUE PIC X(50).
       
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       0000-MAIN.
           PERFORM 1000-EFFICIENT-LOOP
           PERFORM 2000-EFFICIENT-STRING
           PERFORM 3000-EFFICIENT-SEARCH
           PERFORM 4000-EFFICIENT-MOVE
           STOP RUN.
       
       1000-EFFICIENT-LOOP.
      *    BAD: Testing condition each iteration
      *    PERFORM UNTIL WS-EOF = 'Y'
      *
      *    BETTER: Use 88-level condition
           PERFORM UNTIL END-OF-FILE
               CONTINUE
           END-PERFORM
           
      *    BAD: Computing loop limit each time
      *    PERFORM VARYING I FROM 1 BY 1
      *            UNTIL I > FUNCTION LENGTH(WS-STR)
      *
      *    BETTER: Precompute and use COMP variable
           COMPUTE WS-COUNT = FUNCTION LENGTH(WS-OUTPUT-STR)
           PERFORM VARYING WS-INDEX FROM 1 BY 1
                   UNTIL WS-INDEX > WS-COUNT
               CONTINUE
           END-PERFORM
           
      *    BEST: Use reference modification end position
           MOVE WS-OUTPUT-STR(1:WS-STRING-LEN) TO WS-OUTPUT-STR.
       
       2000-EFFICIENT-STRING.
      *    BAD: Multiple STRING operations
      *    STRING A DELIMITED SIZE INTO OUT END-STRING
      *    STRING B DELIMITED SIZE INTO OUT END-STRING
      *
      *    BETTER: Single STRING with all parts
           STRING 'PART1' DELIMITED SIZE
                  '-' DELIMITED SIZE
                  'PART2' DELIMITED SIZE
               INTO WS-OUTPUT-STR
           END-STRING
           
      *    BEST for simple concatenation: Reference modification
           MOVE 'PART1' TO WS-OUTPUT-STR(1:5)
           MOVE '-' TO WS-OUTPUT-STR(6:1)
           MOVE 'PART2' TO WS-OUTPUT-STR(7:5).

      *    BAD: Sequential SEARCH on large table
      *    SET WS-TBL-IDX TO 1
      *    SEARCH WS-ENTRY ...
      *
      *    BETTER: SEARCH ALL (binary search) on sorted table
           SET WS-TBL-IDX TO 1
           SEARCH ALL WS-ENTRY
               AT END
                   CONTINUE
               WHEN WS-LOOKUP-KEY(WS-TBL-IDX) = 'SEARCHKEY'
                   MOVE WS-LOOKUP-VALUE(WS-TBL-IDX) 
                       TO WS-OUTPUT-STR
           END-SEARCH.

      *    BAD: Repeated MOVEs of same value
      *    MOVE SPACES TO FIELD1
      *    MOVE SPACES TO FIELD2
      *    MOVE SPACES TO FIELD3
      *
      *    BETTER: INITIALIZE or group MOVE
           INITIALIZE WS-LOOKUP-TABLE
           
      *    For numeric: Use VALUE clause or INITIALIZE
      *    BAD:  MOVE 0 TO each field
      *    GOOD: INITIALIZE with REPLACING
           INITIALIZE WS-LOOKUP-TABLE
               REPLACING NUMERIC DATA BY ZEROS
               ALPHANUMERIC DATA BY SPACES.

      *    Avoid repeated calculations
      *    BAD:
      *    COMPUTE A = X / 100
      *    COMPUTE B = X / 100 * 1.1
```

What is the difference between PERFORM and PERFORM THRU?

**PERFORM** executes a single paragraph:
```cobol
PERFORM 1000-PROCESS
```

**PERFORM THRU** executes from one paragraph through another (inclusive):
```cobol
PERFORM 1000-PROCESS THRU 1000-EXIT
```

The THRU form is often used with exit paragraphs for early returns:
```cobol
1000-PROCESS.
    IF INVALID-DATA
        GO TO 1000-EXIT
    END-IF
    ... processing ...
1000-EXIT.
    EXIT.
```

Best practice: Use THRU only when you need GO TO within the performed range.
How do I convert numeric to string in COBOL?

Use MOVE with an edited picture:

```cobol
01  WS-NUMBER         PIC S9(7)V99 VALUE -12345.67.
01  WS-DISPLAY        PIC ZZZ,ZZZ.99-.

MOVE WS-NUMBER TO WS-DISPLAY.
* Result: "  12,345.67-"
```

Common edit characters:
- `Z` - Zero suppress (leading zeros become spaces)
- `9` - Always show digit
- `,` - Insert comma
- `.` - Decimal point
- `-` or `CR`/`DB` - Sign indicator
- `$` - Currency symbol

For right-justified with leading zeros:
```cobol
01  WS-NUMERIC        PIC 9(7)V99 VALUE 123.45.
01  WS-STRING         PIC X(10).

MOVE WS-NUMERIC TO WS-STRING.
* Result: "0000123.45" (as zoned decimal)
```
What does FILLER mean in COBOL?

**FILLER** is a reserved word for unnamed data items:

```cobol
01  WS-RECORD.
    05 WS-CUST-ID     PIC X(10).
    05 FILLER         PIC X(5).      *> Unused space
    05 WS-NAME        PIC X(30).
    05 FILLER         PIC X(55).     *> Padding to 100 bytes
```

Uses:
1. **Padding** - Fill space in fixed-length records
2. **Tables** - Define value tables
3. **Skip fields** - Ignore parts of input records

Table example:
```cobol
01  WS-MONTH-TABLE.
    05 FILLER PIC X(9) VALUE 'JANUARY'.
    05 FILLER PIC X(9) VALUE 'FEBRUARY'.
    05 FILLER PIC X(9) VALUE 'MARCH'.
```

FILLER cannot be referenced - it's truly "space filler".

```cobol
01  NI-NAME           PIC S9(4) COMP.  *> Null indicator

EXEC SQL
    SELECT NAME INTO :HV-NAME :NI-NAME
    FROM CUSTOMER WHERE ID = :HV-ID
END-EXEC.

EVALUATE NI-NAME
    WHEN -1      *> NULL
        MOVE '(NO NAME)' TO HV-NAME
    WHEN 0       *> Not null
        CONTINUE
    WHEN OTHER   *> Truncated (value > 0)
        DISPLAY 'NAME TRUNCATED'
END-EVALUATE.
```

Indicator values:
- `-1` = NULL
- `0` = Not null, value fits
- `> 0` = Not null, truncated (value = original length)

Setting NULL on INSERT/UPDATE:
```cobol
MOVE -1 TO NI-NAME.
EXEC SQL UPDATE CUSTOMER SET NAME = :HV-NAME :NI-NAME END-EXEC.
```
What is the difference between STOP RUN and GOBACK?

**STOP RUN** - Terminates the entire run unit:
- Returns control to the operating system
- All programs in the run unit end
- Use in the main program only

**GOBACK** - Returns to the caller:
- In main program: same as STOP RUN
- In subprogram: returns to calling program
- More flexible - works in both contexts

```cobol
*> Main program
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    CALL 'SUBPROG' USING WS-DATA.
    STOP RUN.          *> Or GOBACK - both work

*> Subprogram
PROCEDURE DIVISION USING LS-DATA.
    ... processing ...
    GOBACK.            *> Returns to caller
*   STOP RUN.          *> DON'T - would kill main program!
```

**Best Practice:** Use GOBACK everywhere - it's safer and works in all contexts.
How do I define a COBOL copybook?

A copybook is a separate file containing COBOL code included via COPY:

**CUSTREC.cpy (copybook):**
```cobol
      * Customer Record Layout
       01  CUSTOMER-RECORD.
           05 CUST-ID             PIC X(10).
           05 CUST-NAME           PIC X(50).
           05 CUST-BALANCE        PIC S9(9)V99 COMP-3.
           05 CUST-STATUS         PIC X(1).
               88 CUST-ACTIVE     VALUE 'A'.
               88 CUST-INACTIVE   VALUE 'I'.
```

**Main program:**
```cobol
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       COPY CUSTREC.
```

With REPLACING:
```cobol
       COPY CUSTREC REPLACING ==CUSTOMER== BY ==WS-CUST==.
```

**JCL to compile:**
```jcl
//SYSLIB   DD DSN=YOUR.COPY.LIBRARY,DISP=SHR
```

Copybooks enable code reuse and consistent record layouts across programs.
What are level numbers in COBOL?

Level numbers define data hierarchy (01-49, 66, 77, 88):

```cobol
01  CUSTOMER-REC.              *> 01 = Record level
    05 CUST-NAME.              *> 05 = Group item
       10 FIRST-NAME  PIC X(15). *> 10 = Elementary
       10 LAST-NAME   PIC X(20).
    05 CUST-ADDRESS.
       10 STREET      PIC X(30).
       10 CITY        PIC X(20).
       10 STATE       PIC X(2).
       10 ZIP         PIC X(10).
    05 CUST-BALANCE   PIC S9(7)V99.

66  FULL-NAME RENAMES FIRST-NAME THRU LAST-NAME.  *> RENAMES

77  STANDALONE-FIELD  PIC X(10).  *> Independent item (legacy)

88  IS-POSITIVE VALUE 1 THRU 999. *> Condition name
```

**Level meanings:**
- `01` - Record or independent item
- `02-49` - Subordinate items (usually 05, 10, 15...)
- `66` - RENAMES clause
- `77` - Independent elementary (non-group)
- `88` - Condition name (boolean)

Best practice: Use consistent increments (05, 10, 15) to allow insertion.
How do I read a file sequentially in COBOL?

```cobol
       ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
       INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION.
       FILE-CONTROL.
           SELECT INPUT-FILE ASSIGN TO INFILE
               FILE STATUS IS WS-STATUS.

       DATA DIVISION.
       FILE SECTION.
       FD  INPUT-FILE.
       01  INPUT-RECORD         PIC X(100).

       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01  WS-STATUS            PIC XX.
       01  WS-EOF               PIC X VALUE 'N'.
           88 END-OF-FILE       VALUE 'Y'.

       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           OPEN INPUT INPUT-FILE.
           
           READ INPUT-FILE
               AT END SET END-OF-FILE TO TRUE
           END-READ.
           
           PERFORM UNTIL END-OF-FILE
               DISPLAY INPUT-RECORD
               READ INPUT-FILE
                   AT END SET END-OF-FILE TO TRUE
               END-READ
           END-PERFORM.
           
           CLOSE INPUT-FILE.
           STOP RUN.
```

File status `00` = success, `10` = EOF, `35` = file not found.
What is REDEFINES in COBOL?

**REDEFINES** allows multiple views of the same memory:

```cobol
01  WS-DATE            PIC 9(8) VALUE 20240715.
01  WS-DATE-X REDEFINES WS-DATE.
    05 WS-YEAR         PIC 9(4).
    05 WS-MONTH        PIC 9(2).
    05 WS-DAY          PIC 9(2).

*> WS-DATE = 20240715
*> WS-YEAR = 2024, WS-MONTH = 07, WS-DAY = 15
```

Common uses:

**1. Parse fixed-format records:**
```cobol
01  WS-INPUT           PIC X(100).
01  WS-CUST-REC REDEFINES WS-INPUT.
    05 CR-TYPE         PIC X(2).
    05 CR-DATA         PIC X(98).
```

**2. Type coercion:**
```cobol
01  WS-NUMERIC         PIC S9(9) COMP-3 VALUE 0.
01  WS-BYTES REDEFINES WS-NUMERIC PIC X(5).
```

**3. Union types:**
```cobol
01  WS-AMOUNT          PIC 9(7)V99.
01  WS-AMOUNT-X REDEFINES WS-AMOUNT PIC X(9).
```

Rules:
- Must immediately follow the item being redefined
- Same level number
- Cannot increase size (can be smaller)
How do I use INSPECT in COBOL?

**INSPECT** scans/modifies strings:

**TALLYING - Count occurrences:**
```cobol
01  WS-STRING PIC X(20) VALUE 'ABRACADABRA'.
01  WS-COUNT  PIC 9(3) VALUE 0.

INSPECT WS-STRING TALLYING WS-COUNT FOR ALL 'A'.
*> WS-COUNT = 5

INSPECT WS-STRING TALLYING WS-COUNT 
    FOR LEADING SPACES.
*> Counts leading spaces only

INSPECT WS-STRING TALLYING WS-COUNT
    FOR CHARACTERS BEFORE INITIAL 'C'.
*> Counts chars before first 'C'
```

**REPLACING - Substitute characters:**
```cobol
INSPECT WS-STRING REPLACING ALL 'A' BY 'X'.
*> XBRXCXDXBRX

INSPECT WS-STRING REPLACING FIRST 'A' BY 'Z'.
*> ZBRACADABRA

INSPECT WS-STRING REPLACING LEADING ZEROS BY SPACES.
*> '   12345' from '00012345'
```

**CONVERTING - Character translation:**
```cobol
INSPECT WS-STRING 
    CONVERTING 'ABCD' TO '1234'.
*> All A->1, B->2, C->3, D->4

INSPECT WS-STRING
    CONVERTING 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz'
            TO 'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ'.
*> Uppercase conversion
```

**TALLYING and REPLACING combined:**
```cobol
INSPECT WS-STRING 
    TALLYING WS-COUNT FOR ALL 'X'
    REPLACING ALL 'X' BY 'Y'.
```
What is the difference between VALUE and INITIALIZE?

**VALUE** - Sets initial value at compile time:
```cobol
01  WS-COUNTER   PIC 9(5) VALUE 0.
01  WS-NAME      PIC X(20) VALUE 'DEFAULT'.
01  WS-TABLE     PIC X(10) OCCURS 5 VALUE SPACES.
```

**INITIALIZE** - Resets at runtime:
```cobol
01  WS-RECORD.
    05 WS-NUM    PIC 9(5).
    05 WS-NAME   PIC X(20).
    05 WS-AMT    PIC S9(7)V99 COMP-3.

INITIALIZE WS-RECORD.
*> WS-NUM = 00000
*> WS-NAME = SPACES
*> WS-AMT = 0.00
```

**INITIALIZE with options:**
```cobol
INITIALIZE WS-RECORD
    REPLACING NUMERIC DATA BY 999
    ALPHANUMERIC DATA BY 'X'.

INITIALIZE WS-RECORD
    REPLACING NUMERIC DATA BY ZEROS
    ALPHABETIC DATA BY SPACES.
```

**Key differences:**
| Feature | VALUE | INITIALIZE |
|---------|-------|------------|
| When | Compile time | Runtime |
| Scope | Single item | Group/record |
| Repeatability | Once | Any time |
| FILLER | Can set | Skipped |
How do I do conditional compilation in COBOL?

Use **COPY REPLACING** or **compiler directives**:

**Method 1: COPY REPLACING**
```cobol
*> DEBUGON.cpy
       DISPLAY 'DEBUG: ' WS-VALUE.

*> DEBUGOFF.cpy
       CONTINUE.

*> Main program
       COPY DEBUGON.   *> Or DEBUGOFF for production
```

**Method 2: >>IF directive (Enterprise COBOL)**
```cobol
>>DEFINE DEBUG = 1

       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
>>IF DEBUG = 1
           DISPLAY 'DEBUG MODE ENABLED'.
>>ELSE
           CONTINUE.
>>END-IF
```

**Method 3: Debugging declaratives**
```cobol
       ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
       CONFIGURATION SECTION.
       SOURCE-COMPUTER. IBM-ZOS WITH DEBUGGING MODE.

       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       DECLARATIVES.
       DEBUG-SECTION SECTION.
           USE FOR DEBUGGING ON ALL PROCEDURES.
           DISPLAY 'TRACE: ' DEBUG-NAME.
       END DECLARATIVES.
```

Compile without DEBUG to disable:
```jcl
//COBOL EXEC PGM=IGYCRCTL,PARM='NODEBUG'
```

**Method 4: Runtime flag**
```cobol
01  WS-DEBUG-MODE  PIC X VALUE 'N'.
    88 DEBUG-ON    VALUE 'Y'.

    IF DEBUG-ON
        DISPLAY 'Debug info'
    END-IF.
```
What is USAGE POINTER in COBOL?

**USAGE POINTER** holds memory addresses for dynamic memory and system interfaces:

```cobol
01  WS-PTR            USAGE POINTER.
01  WS-ADDR           USAGE POINTER.
01  WS-DATA-AREA      PIC X(1000).

*> Get address of data area
SET WS-PTR TO ADDRESS OF WS-DATA-AREA.

*> Use address in CALL
CALL 'GETMAIN' USING WS-PTR WS-LENGTH.

*> Set pointer to null
SET WS-PTR TO NULL.

*> Check if null
IF WS-PTR = NULL
    DISPLAY 'Pointer is null'
END-IF.
```

**LINKAGE SECTION usage:**
```cobol
LINKAGE SECTION.
01  LS-PASSED-AREA    PIC X(500).

PROCEDURE DIVISION USING LS-PASSED-AREA.
*> Address is passed automatically

*> Or with pointer:
01  WS-DATA-PTR       USAGE POINTER.
LINKAGE SECTION.
01  LS-DYNAMIC-AREA   PIC X(1000).

PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    CALL 'GETMAIN' USING WS-DATA-PTR WS-LENGTH.
    SET ADDRESS OF LS-DYNAMIC-AREA TO WS-DATA-PTR.
```

**PROCEDURE-POINTER for dynamic calls:**
```cobol
01  WS-PROG-PTR       USAGE PROCEDURE-POINTER.

SET WS-PROG-PTR TO ENTRY 'SUBPROG'.
CALL WS-PROG-PTR USING WS-DATA.
```
How do I handle variable length records in COBOL?

**RECORD CONTAINS ... TO ... CHARACTERS:**

```cobol
       ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
       INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION.
       FILE-CONTROL.
           SELECT VAR-FILE ASSIGN TO VARFILE
               FILE STATUS IS WS-STATUS.
       
       DATA DIVISION.
       FILE SECTION.
       FD  VAR-FILE
           RECORDING MODE IS V
           RECORD CONTAINS 10 TO 1000 CHARACTERS.
       01  VAR-RECORD.
           05 VR-LENGTH           PIC S9(4) COMP.
           05 VR-DATA             PIC X(996).

       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01  WS-ACTUAL-LENGTH       PIC S9(4) COMP.
```

**READ with LENGTH:**
```cobol
READ VAR-FILE INTO WS-RECORD
    LENGTH WS-ACTUAL-LENGTH.
*> WS-ACTUAL-LENGTH contains actual bytes read
```

**WRITE with LENGTH:**
```cobol
MOVE 100 TO WS-ACTUAL-LENGTH.
WRITE VAR-RECORD FROM WS-DATA
    LENGTH WS-ACTUAL-LENGTH.
```

**OCCURS DEPENDING ON for variable tables:**
```cobol
01  WS-VAR-RECORD.
    05 WS-ITEM-COUNT      PIC 9(3).
    05 WS-ITEMS OCCURS 1 TO 100 TIMES
       DEPENDING ON WS-ITEM-COUNT.
       10 WS-ITEM-CODE    PIC X(5).
       10 WS-ITEM-QTY     PIC 9(5).
```

**Spanned records (RECORDING MODE S):**
```cobol
FD  SPAN-FILE
    RECORDING MODE IS S
    RECORD CONTAINS 80 TO 32000 CHARACTERS
    BLOCK CONTAINS 0 RECORDS.
```
What is the ACCEPT statement in COBOL?

**ACCEPT** gets data from system or terminal:

**System information:**
```cobol
01  WS-DATE           PIC 9(8).
01  WS-TIME           PIC 9(8).
01  WS-DAY            PIC 9(7).

ACCEPT WS-DATE FROM DATE YYYYMMDD.     *> 20240715
ACCEPT WS-TIME FROM TIME.              *> 14302156 (HHMMSSCC)
ACCEPT WS-DAY FROM DAY YYYYDDD.        *> 2024197

01  WS-DATE-DATA.
    05 WS-YEAR        PIC 9(4).
    05 WS-MONTH       PIC 9(2).
    05 WS-DAYY        PIC 9(2).
ACCEPT WS-DATE-DATA FROM DATE YYYYMMDD.
```

**Environment variables:**
```cobol
01  WS-ENV-VALUE      PIC X(100).

ACCEPT WS-ENV-VALUE FROM ENVIRONMENT 'HOME'.
ACCEPT WS-ENV-VALUE FROM ENVIRONMENT 'DB_USER'.
```

**Command line arguments:**
```cobol
ACCEPT WS-PARM FROM COMMAND-LINE.
```

**Terminal input (interactive):**
```cobol
01  WS-USER-INPUT     PIC X(80).

DISPLAY 'Enter your name: '.
ACCEPT WS-USER-INPUT.
```

**Day of week:**
```cobol
01  WS-DOW            PIC 9.
ACCEPT WS-DOW FROM DAY-OF-WEEK.  *> 1=Monday, 7=Sunday
```
